opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Sloan (employee ID E043) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E043.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Karen Sloan (E043) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, admin access is permitted per policy. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security check: Karen Sloan (E043) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: Karen Sloan (E043) requests admin access to Payroll. The notes conflict on employment type: Note 1 says full-time (which, as a Payroll Specialist role owner, could permit admin), but Note 2 (Security check) states she is a contractor with basic security training, looked up in the security database. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum for a contractor (read), I grant the maximum: read.
